configure_app.description:
The Media Sync app is installed, but it does not know where to sync yet.

Open **Settings > Apps > Media Sync** and fill in its settings: which server to reach, and which folders to keep in sync. Starting the app once will also create the SSH key you need to give that server.

You can finish here now and set that up afterwards.
configure_app.title: Set up the app

confirm.description:
This adds buttons and status for the Media Sync app, and asks you before anything is deleted while the app's deletion protection is on.

You can start a sync from a dashboard button, from an automation using the Media Sync actions, or by running the script yourself in a terminal. However you start it, the result shows up here.

Transfers run over an encrypted SSH connection, using a key the app creates for itself, so there is no password to store. What gets synced is set up in the app's own settings.
confirm.title: Set up Media Sync

review.description:
The last sync found {count} item(s) that are on one side but not the other, and left them alone.

Something can be missing because it was deleted there, or because it was just added here — there is no way to tell the two apart, so you decide.

**Copy** — the files were added, and the other side should get them.

**Delete** — the files were deleted on purpose, and the side that still has them should let them go.

**There are two ways to choose.** Turn on a toggle to apply that action to *every* folder, or leave it off and tick folders in the list below it. The toggle does not tick the boxes for you — while it is on, the list under it is ignored completely.

A whole run usually goes one way, so the toggles are the short path. Reach for the lists when it does not.

Anything you leave out of both stays pending, so you can decide part of it now and the rest later. Only the items counted here are touched — files already in sync are never affected.
review.title: What should happen?

confirm.description:
The last sync found {count} item(s) that are on one side but not the other, and left them alone.

{deletions}

Something can be missing because it was deleted there, or because it was just added here — there is no way to tell the two apart. If you confirm, the sync runs again and removes these items for good. The list is checked again at that moment, so anything that changed in the meantime is taken into account.

Update the Media Sync app to review these folder by folder and choose what to keep.

init.title: Scheduled checks
init.description:
A convenience, for when all you want is "every so often". Set an interval and a check runs on its own, doing exactly what pressing Sync does.

It is worth having because the remote server cannot announce its own changes — looking on a timer is the only way to notice them.

A check uses the app's settings for everything except direction: the same folders, the same excludes, the same deletion protection, the same test-run switch. It only decides how often, and which way.

Each check compares the whole tree over SSH, so on a large library it costs real time. Watch the "Last run duration" sensor for a few checks before choosing a short interval.

For anything more than a plain interval — only overnight, only when nobody is streaming, or triggered by something else entirely — an automation calling the Media Sync actions gives you the full range. Leave this at 0 and write one of those.

data.check_direction: Which way a check should sync

data_description.check_interval: 0 turns scheduled checks off, which is the default.
data_description.check_direction: Looking for remote changes only needs a pull. Leave it on the app setting to use whatever direction the app itself is configured for.
